findings.summary: this case, on main since d0949f5e6f and carried into the landing by the merge of primary, asserts that queue_order.admission_order raises ValueError on a pointer with no readable queued_at; the change removes that raise and running the file at the reviewed head reproduces 'Failed: DID NOT RAISE ValueError' at line 63 while the sibling case passes, so the landing adds a suite failure on main that neither arm of the run's gate covers.

the dispatch yield check still partitions the queue inline on parse_utc(pointer.get('queued_at')) rather than taking queue_order.partition_placeable, and its comment at lines 473-478 still says 'the ordering keeps its refusal', which the set-aside ordering removed.

the comment above the call the change rewrote still reads 'the ordering refuses such a pointer outright', which reckon/crew/queue_order.py:385-412 no longer does, so it misdescribes the partition_placeable call at selection.py:242 beneath it.

the module docstring's opening paragraph still says the ordering 'refuses a pointer with none', contradicting the closing paragraph this change rewrote and the set-aside behaviour its own cases assert.

the case standing in for the done_when's 'every path that writes a queued pointer' is a static AST scan for a queued_at value copied from another record, so a writer that stamped an unreadable literal, or dropped its stamp, would leave it green.

_restore_queued stamps its restored pointer through readable_queued_at but no test drives _restore_queued, so deleting the stamp would leave every gate green while a restored pointer could be queued unplaceable.
